hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: One aligned read, zero builds: `python tools/gdl/fnasm.py game/ui/select do_player_select 0x27c:0x2e0 --diff` and check whether our `addi rN,r28,712 / add rN,r27,rN` pair sits ABOVE the arm's own `beq`. If at any of the ten sites it sits INSIDE the arm, the hoist is not uniform, the association framing is only half the story, and the sites must be classified before any edit.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: yes - the aligned view was read this pass at 0x80:0xa4, 0x19c:0x1f8, 0x27c:0x2e0, 0x714:0x750, 0x7f8:0x824, 0x1518:0x1548, 0x1af8:0x1b28 and 0x1bd0:0x1c00, and every offset and register above comes from those reads. NOT checked: how `moff` is computed at its definition site, which is exactly what the proposed lever would have to change.
hypothesis.statement: The remaining count deficit of 3 is ONE mechanism repeated ten times, and it is now read from the aligned view rather than the --ops summary (which is what the UE record's hypothesis lacked). The UE record predicted 'the target issues a single `add` where we issue `addi`+`add`'; that is REFUTED - the target issues `add` AND `addi` too, two words either way, and the difference is WHERE and IN WHAT ORDER. Target at each site (quoted from 0x80c-0x814): `add r29,r27,r28` INSIDE the taken arm, then `lwz r0,820(r29)`, then `addi r29,r29,712` - i.e. it forms `page + moff`, folds the +712 into the first load's displacement (820 = 712 + 108), and materialises the pointer afterwards. Ours at the same site (0x800-0x814): `addi r29,r28,712` then `add r29,r27,r29` HOISTED ABOVE the switch dispatch, then `lwz r0,108(r29)` - i.e. it re-associates to `page + (moff + 712)` and hoists the whole thing out of the arm. The same inversion drives the one `lwzx` row: at 0x1b10 the target spills the OFFSET and reads `lwzx r3,r27,r0`, we spill the POINTER and read `lwz r3,0(r3)`. The untried lever is therefore the association, and it must be reached WITHOUT splitting the statement (PROBE 2 measured that and it is catastrophic): the candidate is to change what `moff` is, so that `moff + 712` is not a hoistable loop-invariant - e.g. deriving `moff` at each site from a value the arm already computes rather than from a function-scope accumulator.
